title: Wilson denied need-to-know though the program was funded from his DIA budget

tellings.quote: It's it's that he they claim he didn't have need to know. And that's possible. Uh their budget came from his in other words, their their funding, I'm sorry, their funding came from his director's budget.

plain: In 1997, Thomas R. Wilson, head of the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military intelligence service, was refused details of a secret program on the grounds that he had no "need to know", the security rule that secrets go only to people whose work requires them, even though the program's money came out of his own director's budget. Eric W. Davis, a scientist who has worked on Pentagon projects and says he was part of these events, tells Michels this, allowing that the refusal on paper was "possible". If true, it would mean a program could hide from the very official paying for it.
